name: Andrej Babis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Nicknamed the Czech Donald Trump, Andrej Babis was sworn in as Czech prime minister in December 2025. He previously held the job from December 2017 to December 2021.
His fortune comes from Agrofert, which operates more than 210 companies in everything from  agriculture to renewable energy to media.
The leader of the political party ANO (which means "Yes"), he gave up daily management of Agrofert in 2013.
Prior to the election, he was required to put Agrofert into trusts to comply with a Czech conflict-of-interest law.
Babis got his start as a fertilizer trader. He also worked in Morocco, where he gained experience with foreign trade.
forbes_facts: Babis' wife Monika oversees the Agrofert Foundation, one of the biggest in the Czech Republic.

name: Scott Crabill
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Scott Crabill is a managing partner of software-focused private-equity firm Thoma Bravo, which ranks among the world's top buyout investors.
The firm, with assets of $181 billion, was formed in 2008, when Orlando Bravo and Carl Thoma split from partner Brian Cressey, who was focused on healthcare deals.
Crabill, who holds an MBA from Stanford, led the firm's first software investment, playing a key  role in its evolution as a software buyout specialist
He joined Thoma Bravo in 2002, after stints at Summit Partners and Hewlett-Packard.
His family foundation supports healthcare, education housing and the arts in San Francisco and his childhood hometown of Springfield Ohio.

name: David Wertheim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: David Wertheim is the son of the late Moshe Wertheim (d. 2016), founder of the Central Bottling Company, Israel's Coca Cola bottler. He owns 63% of the company.
Before he died, Moshe Wertheim gave the bottling business, as well as his shares in Mizrahi Tefahot Bank and Alony Hetz,.to David and his sister Drorit,

In 2018, he purchased his billionaire sister's Alony Hetz shares, sold them because of Israeli anti-monopoly rules, and is controlling shareholder of Mizrahi Tefahot, the country's third-largest bank.
He founded and controls Keshet Media Group, which controls TV channel Keshet 12, CH12 News, and websites Mako.co.il and N12.co.il.
He is the founder and CEO of M. Wertheim (Holdings) Ltd., whose investments include publicly traded Alony Hetz Properties & Investments.

name: Mao Lixiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2024); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Mao Lixiang is the founder of Fotile, one of China's largest kitchen appliance brands.
Son Mao Zhongchun currently chairs the business from its headquarters in the eastern Chinese city of Ningbo.
Fotile's top sellers include kitchen range hoods.
Fotile's rivals include Robam Appliances, led by fellow billionaire Ren Jiahua.

name: Xiang Guangda
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Xiang Guangda is the chairman of Tsingshan Holding Group, which has interests in stainless steel, nickel and new energy.
Tsingshan's overseas investments include a nickel ore smelting facility in Indonesia.
It is also building a $233 million plant in Chile for lithium iron phosphate, which is used to power electric vehicles, slated to be commissioned in 2025.
Tsingshan's battery subsidiary Rept Battero Energy went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2023.

name: John Abele
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: John Abele cofounded medical device developer Boston Scientific in 1979 to provide less invasive, more accessible treatments.
Abele took the company public in 1992 and was first listed as a billionaire on The Forbes 400 in 1996.
He served as a director emeritus of the company until 2017, after retiring from the board in 2011 and as co-chairman in 1995.
Abele's Argosy Foundation has doled out more than $130 million to a variety of charitable causes since 2001.
forbes_facts: Abele's father was commander of an American submarine that vanished during World War II. Abele funded an expedition that located the sunken ship in 2007.
Abele received an honorary doctorate of medicine from the University of Vermont in 2018.

name: Semahat Sevim Arsel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025)
forbes_bio: Semahat Sevim Arsel is an heir to the Koc family fortune. She's the oldest member of the clan and the largest shareholder in its main holding company.
Besides energy, automotive, durable consumer goods and finance, Koc is active in technology, food, retail, tourism, agriculture and shipbuilding.
Semahat Arsel serves on the board of Koc Holding and is chairman of its tourism company, Setur. Her husband, Dr. Nusret Arsel, died in 2014 at age 92.
He left all of his wealth to the Vehbi Koc Foundation, named after his father-in-law. Semahat Arsel is president of the foundation.
She also serves as the vice president of the Florence Nightingale Foundation and is the founder of Koc University's School of Nursing.
forbes_facts: She suffered from an extended childhood illness, which later motivated her to establish the Semahat Arsel Nursing Education and Research Centre (SANERC).
Through SANERC, the Vehbi Koc Foundation and the Turkey Education Volunteers Foundation,  which she co-founded, she has impacted many civil society initiatives.

name: Haryanto Tjiptodihardjo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Haryanto Tjiptodihardjo runs listed Impack Pratama Industri, founded in 1981 by his father Handojo.
Headquartered in Jakarta, the company is the country's largest maker of polymer-based roofs by market share and produces other construction materials such as floorboard and pipes.
It also operates manufacturing sites in Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand and Vietnam.
Haryanto joined the company in 1986 after graduating with an MBA degree from Woodbury University in the U.S.
Haryanto sold his privately held Mulford Holdings, an Australia-based plastic sheets maker, to Impack Pratama Industri for 808 billion rupiah ($53 million) in June 2024 to boost the latter's revenue.

name: Evan Spiegel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Evan Spiegel, CEO of Snap Inc., became the world's youngest billionaire at the age of 24 in 2015.
Snap, known for its disappearing photo and video app Snapchat, went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2017.
Spiegel launched the company with Bobby Murphy, a Stanford University fraternity brother, in 2011.
Spiegel and Murphy jointly own just over 20% of Snap but have special voting shares that give them control of the company.
Spiegel graduated from Stanford with a B.S. in product design in 2018, after dropping out to start Snapchat nearly seven years earlier.
forbes_facts: Spiegel grew up in the Los Angeles area and married supermodel Miranda Kerr in the summer of 2017.

name: Timothy Boyle
sec_insider_companies: COLUMBIA SPORTSWEAR CO (COLM) - Chairman, President, CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Timothy Boyle is chairman and CEO of Columbia Sportswear.
The business started as Columbia Hat Company in Portland, founded in 1938 by Boyle's grandparents, who had fled Nazi Germany for the U.S.
Boyle started working at the family business as a college senior, helping his mother run the company after his father's death in 1971.
He is the largest shareholder and has served as CEO since 1988, steering the company to more than $3 billion in annual sales.
forbes_facts: Boyle's mother Gert took charge of the family business as a 46-year-old housewife with three kids. She served as chair for nearly 50 years until she died in 2019.
Boyle has a son and daughter who both work for the company.

name: Paul Saville
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Paul Saville leads Virginia-based NVR, one of the largest homebuilders in the United States, with $10.3 billion in annual revenue.
Saville joined Ryan Homes, now a subsidiary of NVR, in 1981. He became president and CEO in 2005 and was promoted to executive chairman in 2022, taking over for Dwight Schar.
NVR builds homes in 16 states, primarily in the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest.
In 2020, Saville and his wife, Linda, donated $20 million to open a new cancer screening and prevention center in Falls Church, Virginia.
forbes_facts: In 2017, Paul and Linda Saville sold their Palm Beach home to hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin for $85 million.
The Savilles' current residence sits on land previously owned by Donald Trump and Russian oligarch Dmitry Rybolovlev.

name: John McConnell
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2022-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: John P. McConnell is the executive chairman at Worthington Industries, a Columbus, Ohio-based steel processor and producer.
He stepped down as CEO in September 2020, after leading the company for 27 years.
Worthington Industries was founded in 1955 by McConnell's father John H. McConnell (d. 2008).
He's the majority owner of the NHL's Columbus Blue Jackets, a team started by his father in 2000.
McConnell started his career in 1975 as a general laborer in a Worthington steel plant in Louisville, Kentucky.
